subject: Security FAQ update: Audit logging (schema v1, delivery semantics, SIEM export wording)
body:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, Feb 21, 2026 at 9:12 AM PT
Subject: Security FAQ update: Audit logging (schema v1, delivery semantics, SIEM export wording)
Attachments: Redwood_Security_FAQ_Audit_Logging_Draft_2026-02-21.docx

Team — we need to finalize the externally communicable wording for the Security FAQ + enablement deck on audit logging.

Key questions we need alignment on today (so Support + Sales don’t over-promise):

1) Coverage statement: can we say “100% coverage for sensitive admin actions” yet, or do we need to qualify by deployment mode / rollout phase?

2) Delivery semantics: how do we describe at-least-once vs best-effort without creating contractual commitments? (Procurement/legal on the Feb 6 call asked directly about “guaranteed delivery”.)

3) Retention + residency: what’s safe to say about default retention windows and the fact that audit logs exclude payload contents / secrets? We need consistent language with the redaction doc.

4) SIEM export: which targets can we name today (Splunk HEC / Sentinel) vs “supported destinations include …” + roadmap caveat.

I dropped suggested copy in the attached draft (track changes). Please reply with proposed edits + any “do not say” guidance.

Goal: lock by EOD Monday so we can update the shared responses (PM-939) and unblock 2 ongoing security reviews.

— Naomi
Product, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference


---

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, Feb 21, 2026 at 10:03 AM PT
Subject: Re: Security FAQ update: Audit logging (schema v1, delivery semantics, SIEM export wording)

Edits from GRC/evidence perspective:

Coverage wording:
- Please don’t say “100% coverage” without scope qualifiers. Auditors will treat that as universal across all surfaces + all historical versions.
- Suggest: “Redwood emits audit events for sensitive administrative and configuration actions across the Redwood API, Console, control plane, and Private installer/upgrade workflows. Coverage is tracked against a defined sensitive-actions taxonomy and monitored for regressions.”

Delivery semantics:
- Avoid “guaranteed” unless it is explicitly an SLA. Use “designed for at-least-once delivery” and add a sentence on duplicates + de-dupe with event_id.

Retention/residency:
- Recommend stating principles, not specific days, unless we’ve verified the current defaults across Hosted/Dedicated/Private and the contract language.
- “Audit events are designed to minimize PII and never include secrets (e.g., API keys, tokens).”

Also, if we reference SOC 2/ISO control alignment, keep it as “supports common SOC 2 / ISO 27001-aligned controls around logging and monitoring” (not “certified”).

— Olga
GRC

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, Feb 21, 2026 at 11:18 AM PT
Subject: Re: Security FAQ update: Audit logging (schema v1, delivery semantics, SIEM export wording)

+1 to Olga’s guidance.

On delivery semantics, here’s wording I’m comfortable with engineering-wise and that matches our ADR direction:

- “Audit events are delivered with at-least-once semantics. In rare cases (e.g., exporter retries), customers may observe duplicate events and should de-duplicate by event_id.”
- “If an audit sink is temporarily unavailable, the platform buffers and retries delivery; administrative actions continue to function (we do not hard-fail admin workflows solely due to an audit sink outage).”

We should add a single sentence that we have monitoring/alerts on the audit pipeline and an incident runbook, but keep it high level.

On schema: we can say “versioned schema (schema_version) with a documented backcompat policy; exporters normalize legacy events.” That’s safe and aligns with ENG-4827.

If you want I can do a quick inline review of the draft doc text blocks.

— Marcus
Security Engineering

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, Feb 21, 2026 at 12:07 PM PT
Subject: Re: Security FAQ update: Audit logging (schema v1, delivery semantics, SIEM export wording)

On Private-specific statements:

- Please do not imply that every Private customer has SIEM export turned on by default. It’s configurable and depends on the customer’s network + destination.
- Good to say: “Private deployments can be configured to export audit events to customer-controlled SIEM destinations.”

For coverage: we’re close on parity, but not perfect across older Private versions in the field.

Suggest we add a qualifier:
- “Private deployments on supported versions (vX.Y and newer) emit the same audit event types for sensitive actions as Hosted/Dedicated.”

I don’t want to put a version number in the FAQ unless Release confirms. Maybe say “supported versions” and have Support provide specifics if asked.

— Vivek
Product, Private Deployments

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, Feb 21, 2026 at 1:44 PM PT
Subject: Re: Security FAQ update: Audit logging (schema v1, delivery semantics, SIEM export wording)

Agree with the proposed qualifiers.

Two additions I’d like in the FAQ for customer expectation setting:

1) “Audit logs capture who did what, when, and where (actor identity, action type, target resource, source IP where available, and correlation IDs such as request_id/trace_id).”

2) “Audit logs do not include model inputs/outputs by default.” (We should be explicit; it comes up constantly.)

On naming export targets: ok to name Splunk HEC + Azure Sentinel as “currently supported” IF we add “additional destinations via supported HTTP and cloud log sinks; contact support for the current list.”

— Priya
VP Engineering, Platform

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, Feb 21, 2026 at 3:26 PM PT
Subject: Re: Security FAQ update: Audit logging (schema v1, delivery semantics, SIEM export wording)
Attachments: Audit_Log_Schema_v1_External_Snippet_2026-02-21.pdf

Thanks — I’ll incorporate.

Proposed final external wording (for agreement):

A) Coverage
“Redwood emits audit events for sensitive administrative and configuration actions across the Redwood API, Console, control plane services (e.g., RBAC and credential lifecycle), routing/policy configuration, and Private installer/upgrade workflows. Coverage is defined by a published sensitive-actions taxonomy and monitored for regressions.”

B) Semantics
“Audit events are designed for at-least-once delivery. In rare cases, customers may observe duplicate events (e.g., due to retry behavior) and can de-duplicate using event_id.”

C) Data minimization
“Audit events are designed to minimize PII and do not include secrets (e.g., API keys, tokens) or model prompts/responses by default.”

D) Schema/backcompat
“Audit events follow a versioned schema (schema_version) with a documented compatibility policy. Exporters normalize events so customers can consume consistent fields over time.”

E) Export
“Hosted and Private deployments can be configured to export audit events to customer-controlled systems. Supported targets include Splunk (HEC) and Azure Sentinel, with additional options available depending on deployment.”

Please reply with any objections, especially to (B) and (E). I attached a 1-pager schema snippet we can share in reviews (field list + example event) — no internal links.

Also confirming: we will NOT use the phrase “guaranteed delivery” anywhere.

— Naomi

Subject: Re: Security FAQ update: Audit logging (schema v1, delivery semantics, SIEM export wording)

No objections.

Minor tweak suggestion on (B) to reduce “rare cases” debate:
- Replace “In rare cases” with “Customers may observe duplicate events…” and leave it at that.

Everything else looks good + appropriately scoped.

— Marcus
